rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali says the Prophet is on clear proof and he is its confirming witness; al-Mufid, al-Ayyashi, Ibn Shahr Ashub, and Sunni collectors transmit variants.
rows.anchor: فرسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم على بينة من ربه وأنا الشاهد له ومنه

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet identifies himself as the one on clear proof and Ali as the witness who follows him.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم { أفمن كان على بينة من ربه } أنا { ويتلوه شاهد منه } قال علي

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abu Ja‘far identifies Ali, rather than Ibn Salam, as the one with knowledge of the Book and connects three Qur’anic descriptions to him.
rows.anchor: قال أبو مريم حدث علينا الحديث الذي حدثتني به عن أبي جعفر قال كنت عند أبي جعفر جالسا إذ مر علينا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Reports through Ibn Abbas identify Ali as the witness to the Prophet, including a version that calls him the witness specifically.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس هو علي يشهد للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو منه

rows.speaker: صاحب المنار
rows.claim: Al-Manar says Shi‘i interpreters identify the witness as Ali in support of Imamate, while another report has Ali interpret it as the Prophet’s tongue; opponents identify Abu Bakr, and he calls both readings partisan.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب المنار في تفسير الآية عند ذكر معاني الشاهد ومنها أنه علي رضي الله عنه ترويه الشيعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabatabai rejects al-Manar’s charge that the Ali interpretation is merely partisan: its transmitters are more numerous among Sunnis than Shi‘is, and the preceding discussion answers the Abu Bakr analogy.
rows.anchor: أما قوله إن الشيعة ترويه فقد عرفت أن رواته من أهل السنة أكثر من الشيعة

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abu Abdillah explains the name Kulaib Taslim: submission is humble surrender to God, as the Qur’an describes believers who are humble before their Lord.
rows.anchor: قال هو والله الإخبات قول الله عز وجل { الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات وأخبتوا إلى ربهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob’s conspicuous love and protection of Joseph and Benjamin intensified their brothers’ envy; his warning to conceal the dream was overtaken by destiny.
rows.anchor: وكان يخافهم عليه ولا يرضى بخلوتهم به ولا يأمنهم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers call Jacob astray in social judgment because they think he wrongly prefers two young, weak sons over their capable, strong collective.
rows.anchor: ولم يريدوا برمي أبيهم بالضلال الضلال في الدين حتى يكفروا بذلك بل الضلال في مشيئته الاجتماعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabatabai rejects the claim that the brothers’ accusation is simply an ignorant demand for equal treatment, caused by Jacob’s excessive love for their mother; he reads their jealousy in the family conflict described above.
rows.anchor: ما في مختلف التفاسير من الانحراف في تقرير معنى الآية منها ما ذكره بعضهم أن هذا الحكم منهم بضلال أبيهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: An unnamed interpretation says Jacob knowingly let affection for Joseph override his duty to raise his children justly, while excusing this as an irresistible attachment.
rows.anchor: وأما قوله وما كان يعقوب يخفى عليه هذا إلى آخر ما قال ومعناه أن هوى يعقوب في ابنه صرفه عن الواجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabatabai rejects this account as undermining moral responsibility: human beings can cultivate virtue and suppress ego-driven vice, so religious commands against following desire would otherwise be pointless.
rows.anchor: أن الإنسان بحسب فطرته في سعة من التخلق بها ومحق الرذائل النفسانية التي أصلها وأساسها اتباع هوى النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets such as Jacob are divinely guided, chosen, and devoted to God; they seek only truth and God’s pleasure, not their own desires.
rows.anchor: فاخبر أنه هداهم إلى مستقيم صراطه ولم يقيد ذلك بقيد، وأنه اجتباهم وجمعهم وأخلصهم لنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise to inform the brothers means Joseph will verbally reveal what they did; his later question, “Did you know what you did to Joseph?”, confirms that reading, while “unaware” parallels “not sensing.”
rows.anchor: وقوله { إذ أنتم جاهلون } فإنه يحاذي من هذه الآية التي نحن فيها قوله { وهم لا يشعرون }

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One alternative says Joseph will tell his brothers what they did when they later meet him without recognizing him in Egypt.
rows.anchor: وهو الذي أخبرهم به في مصر وهم لا يعرفونه ثم عرفهم نفسه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another reading takes “inform them” as a threat-like idiom for requiting them for their wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: ومنها أن المراد بإنبائه إياهم مجازاتهم بسوء ما علوا كمن يتوعد من أساء إليه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says Joseph recognized his brothers in Egypt and used a cup to divine that they had cast away and sold their paternal brother.
rows.anchor: كما روي عن ابن عباس أن المراد بإنبائه إياهم بأمرهم ما جرى له مع إخوته بمصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabatabai calls these first alternatives weak and prefers the direct verbal disclosure supported by Joseph’s later words.
rows.anchor: وهذه وجوه لا تخلو من سخافة والوجه ما قدمناه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view says God’s revelation itself told Joseph that he would inform his brothers, who would remain unaware of the revelation; Tabatabai considers it possible but sees no reason for that qualifier.
rows.anchor: ومنها قول بعضهم إن المعنى وأوحينا إليه ستخبرهم بما فعلوا بك وهم لا يشعرون بهذا الوحي

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpret the promise as Joseph’s later rise in status and kingship over his brothers; Tabatabai rejects the shift from verbal disclosure to visible circumstances because the later dialogue explicitly states what he told them.
rows.anchor: وعمدة الفرق بين هذا القول وما قدمناه من الوجه أن في هذا القول صرف الإنباء عن الإنباء الكلامي إلى الإنباء بالحال الخارجي والوضع العيني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Evening” means the end of the day, or the period from sunset prayer until night; the brothers wept to disguise their plot and win their father’s trust.
rows.anchor: العشاء آخر النهار، وقيل من صلاة المغرب إلى العتمة، وإنما كانوا يبكون ليلبسوا الأمر على أبيهم

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines sabq as preceding in movement and istibaq as racing or competing.
rows.anchor: أصل السبق التقدم في السير نحو { والسابقات سبقا } والاستباق التسابق

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari glosses “we went to race” as racing in running or archery, noting that the reciprocal and reflexive forms can overlap.
rows.anchor: نستبق أي نتسابق، والافتعال والتفاعل يشتركان كالانتضال والتناضل

rows.speaker: صاحب المنار
rows.claim: Al-Manar distinguishes istibaq as striving to get ahead from reciprocal competition, applying this to the brothers’ race and contrasting it with good deeds and the race to the door.
rows.anchor: إنا ذهبنا نستبق أي ذهبنا من مكان اجتماعنا إلى السباق يتكلف كل منا أن يسبق غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabatabai rejects al-Manar’s distinction: “race for good deeds” and the race to the door also involve each party trying to get ahead, so istibaq and tasabuq coincide in use.
rows.anchor: فالحق أن معنيي الاستباق والتسابق متحدان صدقا على المورد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reflexive form emphasizes the agent’s effort to secure precedence for himself; because precedence is comparative, this effort entails racing against others.
rows.anchor: وزنة " افتعل " تفيد تأكد معنى " فعل " وإمعان الفاعل في فعله وأخذه حلية لنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A believer in us” means someone who accepts their account; iman can take either the preposition li or bi, as in the verse about Lot.
rows.anchor: وقوله { بمؤمن لنا } أي بمصدق لقولنا، والإيمان يتعدى باللام كما يتعدى بالباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers claim they went into the open country to race, probably on foot, leaving Joseph with their belongings, where a wolf supposedly ate him.
rows.anchor: ذهبنا إلى البيداء نتسابق في عدو أو رمي - ولعله كان في عدو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their admission that Jacob would not believe them even if truthful is an excuse formula used when one has run out of means; it indirectly signals that their account is true.
rows.anchor: وقولهم { وما أنت بمؤمن لنا ولو كنا صادقين } كلام يأتي بمثله المعتذر إذا انقطع عن الأسباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “lying blood” uses the verbal noun as an emphatic active description, meaning blood that clearly lies about the alleged attack.
rows.anchor: الكذب بالفتح فالكسر مصدر أريد به الفاعل للمبالغة أي بدم كاذب بين الكذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite, scant blood had little evidentiary force; an intact shirt contradicts their story because a devouring beast would have torn it.
rows.anchor: فإن من افترسته السباع وأكلته لم تترك له قميصا سالما غير ممزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deception cannot keep its credibility: contradictions within a lie or surrounding evidence eventually reveal it.
rows.anchor: من المجرب أن الكذب لا يدوم على اعتباره وأن الكاذب لا يلبث دون أن يأتي بما يكذبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because events form an interconnected order of fixed relations and consequences, disguising one fact cannot conceal all its implications; truth ultimately prevails despite temporary falsehood.
rows.anchor: أن الكون يجري على نظام يرتبط به بعض أجزائه ببعض بنسب وإضافات غير متغيرة ولا متبدلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob denies the wolf story: the brothers’ own selves had made some scheme attractive to them, and his unspecific wording both accuses and avoids naming their deed.
rows.anchor: والتسويل الوسوسة أي ليس الأمر على ما تخبرون بل وسوست لكم أنفسكم فيه أمرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Beautiful patience” praises patience by naming the cause for its result; its indefinite form and omitted adjective suggest either its grandeur or its bitterness and difficulty.
rows.anchor: وقوله { فصبر جميل } مدح للصبر وهو من قبيل وضع السبب موضع المسبب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The circumstances leave Jacob with no practical path but patience: his beloved son is said to be dead, he sees the brothers’ lie, and his only powerful helpers are the suspected perpetrators.
rows.anchor: فلا يسعه إلا الصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience is not passive submission to abuse; it is inner steadiness and clear judgment, while people remain properly equipped to resist harm as far as they can.
rows.anchor: بل الصبر هو الاستقامة في القلب وحفظ النظام النفساني الذي به يستقيم أمر الحياة الإنسانية من الاختلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The patient remain upright under calamity rather than fleeing at its first assault; patience protects inner order and sound deliberation.
rows.anchor: فالصابرون هم القائمون في النوائب على ساق لا تزيلهم هجمات المكاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience is a defensive fortress, but recovery needs a further cause; in monotheism that cause is God, so one first preserves inner devotion and then entrusts the outcome to Him.
rows.anchor: وهذا السبب في ملة التوحيد هو الله عز سلطانه فعلى الإنسان الموحد إذا نابته نائبة ونزلت عليه مصيبة أن يتحصن أولا بالصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob completes patience with trust in God, just as he later says he hopes God will bring his sons back together.
rows.anchor: ولهذا كله لما قال يعقوب عليه السلام { فصبر جميل } عقبه بقوله { والله المستعان على ما تصفون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob knows the brothers plotted and that the wolf story is false, yet asks God alone to expose their claim and restore Joseph rather than relying on outward causes independently.
rows.anchor: أني أعلم أن لكم في الأمر مكرا وأن يوسف لم يأكله ذئب لكنى لا أركن في كشف كذبكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “God is the one sought for help” is a prayer expressing exclusive divine agency: Jacob omits himself and submits the matter to God’s rightful rule.
rows.anchor: والكلمة مبنية على توحيد الفعل فإنها مسوقة سوق الحصر ومعناها أن الله سبحانه هو المستعان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even in grief, Jacob’s love for Joseph and sorrow at losing him are wholly for God’s sake, not self-centered attachment.
rows.anchor: غير أنه ما كان يحب يوسف ولا يتوله فيه ولا يجد لفقده إلا لله وفي الله

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين عليهما السلام
rows.claim: A report reproaches Jacob for failing to feed the devout stranger Dmyal despite having surplus food; God says mercy to the needy is beloved and trials reach His friends sooner as care, while enemies are gradually ensnared.
rows.anchor: يا يعقوب ما رحمت دميال عبدي المجتهد في عبادته القانع باليسير من ظاهر الدنيا

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين عليهما السلام
rows.claim: The report places Joseph’s dream on the same night that Jacob’s household ate fully while Dmyal went hungry; Jacob warned Joseph not to tell his brothers, but he did, and their first envy followed.
rows.anchor: قال علي بن الحسين عليهما السلام إن أول بلوى نزل بيعقوب وآل يعقوب الحسد ليوسف لما سمعوا منه الرؤيا

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين عليهما السلام
rows.claim: Jacob’s fear that the trial concerned Joseph made him especially tender toward him; after the brothers’ jealousy grew, he reluctantly handed Joseph over while anticipating the test.
rows.anchor: فدفعه إليهم وهو لذلك كاره متوقع البلوى من الله في يوسف

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report classifies prophets by how revelation reaches them: some hear a sound, some receive dreams as Joseph and Abraham did, some see directly, and some receive inspiration in the heart and ear.
rows.anchor: عن زرارة عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال الأنبياء على خمسة أنواع منهم من يسمع

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Umar transmits the Prophet’s description of Joseph as the noble son of a noble line: Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham.
rows.anchor: أخرج أحمد والبخاري عن ابن عمر أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report says Jacob was tested because he slaughtered a fat ram while a needy companion had no food to break his fast; afterward Jacob arranged public lunches and dinners.
rows.anchor: عن أبي خديجة عن رجل عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال انما ابتلي يعقوب بيوسف أنه ذبح كبشا

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Through Abu al-Jarud, Abu Ja‘far explains that the brothers would not realize the man speaking to them was Joseph; Gabriel had informed him.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في قوله { لتنبئنهم بأمرهم هذا وهم لا يشعرون }

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report attributed through Abu al-Jarud says the brothers slaughtered a young goat on Joseph’s shirt to make the bloodstain.
rows.anchor: وفيه وفي رواية أبي الجارود في قول الله { وجاؤا على قميصه بدم كذب } قال إنهم ذبحوا جديا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tusi’s report glosses beautiful patience as patience without complaint; Tabatabai guesses it comes from al-Sadiq and notes a similar Prophetic report from Hayyan ibn Jabala.
rows.anchor: وفي أمالي الشيخ بإسناده في قوله عز وجل { فصبر جميل } قال بلا شكوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation unfolds through stages toward its final end, which is return to God; a purposeless act is false, and an ordered but pointless act is play.
rows.anchor: فلا تزال الخلقة تقع مرحلة بعد مرحلة وتنال غاية بعد غاية حتى تتوقف في غاية لا غاية بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s creation must be true and purposeful, leading to an abiding world; otherwise the ordered universe would be purposeless play suggesting a need for relief or amusement, impossible for the self-sufficient God.
rows.anchor: وفعله تعالى ملازم للحق مصاحب له فخلق السماوات والأرض يخلف عالما باقيا بعد زواله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “created in truth,” the preposition bi indicates accompaniment; Tabatabai rejects causal, instrumental, or purposive readings.
rows.anchor: أن الباء في قوله { بالحق } للمصاحبة وأن قول بعضهم أن الباء للسببية أو الآلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s ability to remove people and bring a new creation is not difficult; the address to all humanity uses the Prophet as its representative.
rows.anchor: والخطاب لعامة البشر بجعل النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم مثالا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The possibility of replacing creation shows it is not play: God is self-sufficient, and the replacement verse explains the purposeful order introduced by the question about creation.
rows.anchor: ولعل هذه النكتة هي التي أوجبت تعقيب قوله { كيف خلق الله السماوات والأرض } بقوله { إن يشأ يذهبكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using the explicit name Allah in “not difficult for Allah” underscores the proof: this is easy precisely because He is God.
rows.anchor: وضع الظاهر في موضع المضمر في قوله { على الله } للدلالة على الحجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although removing some humans while leaving the world unchanged could be pointless, the verse describes removing people and bringing replacements into the integrated creation.
rows.anchor: ولو أذهب الناس على بقاء من السماوات والأرض بحالها الحاضرة كان ذلك باطلا ولعبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Removing people alone while preserving the rest of the world would also be play; the true replacement is one people by others within a complete creation.
rows.anchor: إذهاب الإنسان فقط من غير إتيان بخلق جديد على إبقاء لسائر الخلق المشهود لعب باطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lexically, baraz means emerge into open space; tabi can be a plural, collective noun, or emphatic verbal noun; ighna means benefit and carries a sense of warding off; jaza opposes patience; mahis is an escape place.
rows.anchor: والتبع بفتحتين جمع تابع كخدم وخادم، وقيل اسم جمع، وقيل مصدر جيء به للمبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At resurrection, people appear to God without the barriers they imagined in life; God was never hidden from them, as the Qur’an states.
rows.anchor: وهذا بالنسبة إلى أنفسهم حيث كانوا يتوهمون في الدنيا إن ربهم في غيبة عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, appearing before God is a metaphor for being wholly subject to judgment and the execution of the promised recompense.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن تكون الجملة كناية عن خلوصهم لحساب الأعمال وتعلق المشيئة الإلهية بانقطاع الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The weak are blind followers and the arrogant are their powerful unbelieving leaders; the followers ask whether their leaders can now ward off any punishment.
rows.anchor: فالضعفاء هم المقلدون المطيعون لأوليائهم من الكفار، والمستكبرون هم أولياؤهم المتبوعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “some of God’s punishment,” min is explanatory, while in “anything” it is emphatic; the leaders’ answer may concern escape from punishment or guidance to faith, since the afterlife reveals worldly realities.
rows.anchor: ظاهر السياق أن المراد بالهداية هنا الهداية إلى طريق التخلص من العذاب ويمكن أن يكون المراد بها الهداية إلى الدين الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “It is the same for us whether we grieve or endure; there is no escape” treats both reactions as equal because their unavoidable punishment leaves no way out.
rows.anchor: وسواء خبر لمبتدأ محذوف والجملة الاستفهامية بيان لذلك، وقوله { ما لنا من محيص } بيان آخر

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majma‘ glosses israk as answering a cry for help with rescue.
rows.anchor: في المجمع الإصراخ الإغاثة بإجابة الصارخ ويقال استصرخني فلان فأصرخته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The devil’s speech at judgment exposes the true relation between him and his followers; God promised their disagreements would be clarified, and every false object or leader will disown them.
rows.anchor: وهذا كلام جامع يلقيه الشيطان يوم القيامة إلى الظالمين يبين فيه موقعه منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although shaytan can mean any rebellious human or jinn, the speaker here is Iblis, the source of human misguidance, who vowed to mislead people and is shown inviting them to shirk.
rows.anchor: والشيطان وإن كان بمعنى الشرير وربما أطلق في كلامه تعالى على كل شرير من الجن والإنس

rows.speaker: إبليس
rows.claim: Iblis says God’s promise was true and fulfilled in resurrection, judgment, Paradise, and Hell, while his own promise that none of these would occur proved false.
rows.anchor: فقوله إن الله وعدكم وعد الحق { ووعدتكم فأخلفتكم } أي وعدكم الله وعدا حققه الوقوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s references to Iblis’s offspring and clan show that other devils may assist in misleading some people or particular actions, but all misguidance ultimately traces to Iblis.
rows.anchor: فولاية الواحد منهم إما لبعض الناس دون بعض أو في بعض الأعمال دون بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis’s purpose is to shift blame for sin to the listeners and disavow their partnership; God’s promise came true, whereas Iblis’s denial of the afterlife was exposed as false.
rows.anchor: يريد بكلامه رد اللوم على فعل المعاصي إليهم والتبري من شركهم

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators take God’s promise and Iblis’s counter-promise as referring to the afterlife; the broken promise is a metonym for the lie being exposed.
rows.anchor: كذا ذكره المفسرون. وعلى هذا فالموعود جميع ما يرجع إلى المعاد إثباتا ونفيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabatabai broadens the promises to cover worldly and afterlife results: faith brings a good life and shirk a constricted one, followed by resurrection and judgment.
rows.anchor: ومن الممكن - بل هو الوجه - أن يشمل الوعد ما يترتب على الإيمان والشرك في الدنيا والآخرة جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis promises pleasant desires and long hopes, distracts people from death and judgment, and makes them fear poverty and blame; his method is to make worldly causes and the self seem independently powerful.
rows.anchor: وكان مفتاحه في جميع ذلك إغفالهم عن مقام ربهم وتزيين ما بين أيديهم من الأسباب مستقلة بالتأثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s promises about both worlds are fulfilled, while Iblis sells fantasies that people either never attain or find disappointing once attained.
rows.anchor: وهي بين ما لا يناله الإنسان قطعا وما إذا ناله وجده غير ما كان يظنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited passage calls Satan’s promises delusion and says God’s servants are beyond his authority.
rows.anchor: وعدهم وما يعدهم الشيطان إلا غرورا إن عبادي ليس لك عليهم سلطان

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi understands Satan’s whispering as a kind of control, distinct from physical force.
rows.anchor: ما كان لي تسلط عليكم إلا بالوسوسة لا بالضرب ونحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The followers themselves control their actions and so bear responsibility for their choices.
rows.anchor: لأن لكم السلطان على عملكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception “except that I called you” is disconnected: Iblis merely invited people to sin and had no authority over them; permission to invite is not coercion.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر سقوط ما وجه به الرازي في تفسيره كون الاستثناء متصلا

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi reads the exception as connected: Satan’s whispering strengthens desire and is a kind of power, even without physical force.
rows.anchor: وجه السقوط أن عدم كون مجرد الدعوة سلطانا وتمكنا من القهر على المدعو بديهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabatabai says desire and submission arise from the followers themselves; Iblis denies power he owns, not power they voluntarily grant him, as “blame yourselves” confirms.
rows.anchor: هي سلطة يملكها المدعو من نفسه فيملكها الداعي وليس الداعي يملكها عليه من نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an says Satan’s authority follows people’s willing allegiance and association, rather than causing it; the negative “no authority at all” leaves blame with them.
rows.anchor: والآيات - كما ترى - ظاهرة في أن سلطانه متفرع على الاتباع والتولي والإشراك لا بالعكس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “I cannot rescue you and you cannot rescue me” means neither side can deliver or intercede for the other.
rows.anchor: أي ما أنا بمغيثكم ومنجيكم وما أنتم بمغيثي ومنجي فلا أنا شافع لكم ولا أنتم شافعون لي اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an describes following Satan as worship, clarifying how Iblis can disavow the partnership of those who followed him.
rows.anchor: ألم أعهد إليكم يا بني آدم أن لا تعبدوا الشيطان إنه لكم عدو مبين وأن اعبدوني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis’s repudiation parallels the Qur’anic accounts of false gods and leaders disowning those who followed them.
rows.anchor: وهذا الكلام منه تبر من شركهم كما حكى سبحانه تبري كل متبوع باطل من تابعه يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration that wrongdoers face painful punishment completes Iblis’s speech: they wronged themselves and merit that consequence.
rows.anchor: وقوله { إن الظالمين لهم عذاب أليم } من تمام كلام إبليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Neither can you rescue me” implies the bond between Iblis and followers has ended; otherwise it would be needless. Their earthly following provides no tie or aid now.
rows.anchor: وظاهر السياق أن قوله { ما أنا بمصرخكم وما أنتم بمصرخي } كناية عن انتفاء الرابطة بينه وبين تابعيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The followers blame Iblis expecting solidarity in punishment, but he disowns them and will not approach them because they are wrongdoers facing painful punishment.
rows.anchor: فهو قريب المعنى من قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers’ greetings of peace in Paradise contrast with the disputation, accusation, and despair among the condemned in the preceding verses.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله { تحيتهم فيها سلام } مقابلة حالهم من انعكاس السلام والتحية المباركة من بعضهم إلى بعض

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One grammatical analysis makes “a good word” an apposition of inclusion to “example,” with “like a good tree” as its modifier or as a predicate of an omitted subject.
rows.anchor: ذكروا أن " كلمة " بدل اشتمال من " مثلا " و " كشجرة " صفة بعد صفة لقوله " كلمة "

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A second analysis makes “word” the delayed first object of daraba and moves “example” ahead of its adjective to avoid separating the word from “like a tree.”
rows.anchor: وقيل إن " كلمة " مفعول أول متأخر لضرب و " مثلا " مفعوله الثاني قدم لدفع محذور الفصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabatabai prefers taking daraba with one object and construing “word” as the explanatory statement of the whole comparison, with an implied verb meaning “made it like a tree.”
rows.anchor: وأظن أن هذا أحسن الوجوه لو وجه بكون " كلمة طيبة " الخ عطف بيان لقوله { ضرب الله مثلا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tree’s root is firmly embedded in earth, its branches rise skyward, and it bears edible fruit continually by God’s permission.
rows.anchor: وقوله { تؤتي أكلها كل حين بإذن ربها } أي تثمر ثمرها المأكول كل زمان بإذن الله

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Reported meanings of the good word include the testimony of unity, faith, Qur’an, praise or glorification, every good word, all obedience, and the believer.
rows.anchor: فقيل هي شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله، وقيل الإيمان، وقيل القرآن، وقيل مطلق التسبيح والتنزيه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Reported good-tree identifications include the date palm, coconut, any tree with wholesome fruit, or a hypothetical tree with the stated qualities.
rows.anchor: فقيل النخلة وهو قول الأكثرين، وقيل شجرة جوز الهند، وقيل كل شجرة تثمر ثمرة طيبة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Exegetes variously define the fruit-bearing “time” as two months, six months, a year, each morning and evening, or all times.
rows.anchor: ثم اختلفوا في المراد بالحين فقيل شهران، وقيل ستة أشهر، وقيل سنة كاملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fruitfulness image prepares the contrast between the peaceful reward of believers and the earlier conflict among the damned.
rows.anchor: مع حال غيرهم المذكورين في الآيتين السابقتين من الخصام وتجبيه بعضهم بعضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Context identifies the good word as firm true belief: the next verse describes God establishing believers by the firm word, which is a statement grounded in conviction and resolve.
rows.anchor: والذي يعطيه التدبر في الآيات أن المراد بالكلمة الطيبة التي شبهت بشجرة طيبة من صفتها كذا وكذا هو الاعتقاد الحق الثابت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is not sound alone but tawhid confessed and followed consistently; related verses pair professing God’s lordship with steadfastness and good works.
rows.anchor: ولا كل كلمة بما هي لفظ بل بما هي معتمدة على اعتقاد وعزم يستقيم عليه الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawhid is the fixed root from which true beliefs, good morals, and righteous deeds branch; these sustain human life and fit the order of creation.
rows.anchor: وله فروع نشأت ونمت من غير عائق يعوقه عن ذلك من عقائد حقة فرعية وأخلاق زاكية وأعمال صالحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Perfect believers continually benefit others like a fruitful tree; the same pattern applies to every true statement and righteous deed, though the verse’s contextual root is tawhid.
rows.anchor: وكذلك كل كلمة حقة وكل عمل صالح مثله هذا المثل، له أصل ثابت وفروع رشيدة وثمرات طيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable urges people seeking happiness to realize tawhid and remain steadfast in it.
rows.anchor: ليتذكر به المتذكر أن لا محيص لمريد السعادة عن التحقق بكلمة التوحيد والاستقامة عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ijtithath means uprooting; the related nouns denote an elevated mound and an outwardly projecting body.
rows.anchor: الاجتثاث الاقتلاع، يقال جثته واجتثته أي قلعته واقتلعته

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Commentators give opposing meanings for the bad word and bad tree: shirk’s opposite readings, and trees such as colocynth, dodder, garlic, thorn, algae, truffle, or any tree with bad fruit.
rows.anchor: فقيل هي الحنظلة، وقيل الكشوث وهو نبت يلتف على الشوك والشجر لا أصل له في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bad word is shirk, represented by a tree uprooted without a firm root or foothold; its only effects are harm and evil.
rows.anchor: فإنما هي كلمة الشرك مثلت بشجرة خبيثة مفروضة اقتلعت من فوق الأرض ليس لها أصل ثابت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “by the firm word” modifies God’s establishing, not the believers’ believing; bi means instrument or cause, while “in this life and the next” also modifies establishing.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن " بالقول " متعلق بقوله " يثبت " لا بقوله " آمنوا " ، والباء للآلة أو السببية لا للتعدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s steadying of believers parallels His misguiding of those who deviate, but guidance begins with God whereas punitive misguidance follows a person’s chosen deviation.
rows.anchor: فيعود المعنى إلى أن الذين آمنوا إذا ثبتوا على إيمانهم واستقاموا ثبتهم الله عليه في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God first creates humans with sound nature and recognition of lordship, then supports it through prophetic teaching; following that nature leads to faith by divine guidance.
rows.anchor: خلق الإنسان على فطرة سليمة ركز فيها معرفة ربوبيته وألهمها فجورها وتقواها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who voluntarily abandon their sound nature and resist truth become astray through their own choice; God then punishes by withdrawing mercy and success.
rows.anchor: فهو ضلال منه غير مسبوق بإضلال من الله وحاشاه سبحانه - لكنه يستعقب إضلاله عن الطريق مجازاة
